text:
A: Hey! There we go. Hi, I'm Callum.
B: Hi, Gemma.
A: Gemma, nice one. How was the puzzle bit? I absolutely bombed that, I'm not gonna lie.
B: It was fine. I finished it.
A: All of it? Fair play. I got to the shapes ones and my brain just sort of left the building. So what do you do, Gemma?
B: New car sales. Franchised dealership in Basingstoke.
A: No way! Stop it. I'm in car sales. Used and nearly-new, outside Stevenage.
B: Oh right. Funny. Used's a different game, though.
A: Yeah, yeah, totally different game. You've got the manufacturer behind you, the shiny showroom, all that. We've got a forecourt on an industrial estate and a bloke who does the valeting with a hose.
B: We've got targets from the manufacturer on top of ours, so it's not exactly easy either. How are you doing this month?
A: Erm, decent, yeah. I'm usually near the top of the board. This month's a bit slow, to be honest, it's been quiet on the forecourt.
B: I'm top this month. Second last month, by one car, which I'm still annoyed about.
A: By one car! That's brutal. Who beat you?
B: New lad. He got a fleet deal handed to him, so it doesn't really count, to be fair.
A: It doesn't count, no, a handed fleet deal is basically cheating. I'd be fuming.
B: I was.
A: Ha. Erm, so, do you do Saturdays? I'm six days most weeks, Saturdays are a killer.
B: Alternate ones. I'm off this weekend, thank God.
A: Lucky. What do you do on your days off then? Let me guess, gym. I clocked the top in your photo.
B: Gym, yeah, three times a week. Weights and rowing. And I walk the dog. I did the Basingstoke Half last year, two hours four.
A: Two hours four, that's proper. I couldn't do half of a half. I've been playing padel with a couple of lads from work, and honestly, mate, padel is way harder than it looks. You think it's just tennis for people who've given up, then you're on the floor.
B: I've never played it.
A: You'd smash it, honestly, with the rowing and that. You'd have the arms for it.
B: Maybe.
A: Yeah. Erm... so what are you watching at the minute? I watched this Korean thriller last night, it was unreal, like proper twisty, there's this—
B: I don't really do subtitles. I'm watching The Traitors.
A: The Traitors, okay, yeah, everyone's on that.
B: I'd win it. Honestly. It's just reading people, which is what we do all day.
A: That's a good shout, actually. We'd be well suited, car salespeople. You'd know straight away who's lying.
B: I'd know who's lying in about five seconds, yeah.
A: Bit worrying for me, then.
B: Is it?
A: Ha! No, no. I'm an open book. Ask my mum. Erm, do you reckon you'll stay in sales, or go for manager?
B: Manager. If they don't give it me in the next couple of years I'll go to another group. I'm not loyal for the sake of it.
A: Nah, fair. Same, I'd love a premium brand, the commission on those—
B: The commission's better, but the customers are worse.
A: The customers are worse, ha, I can imagine. I had a bloke yesterday test-drive a car just to get to Tesco—
